subject: Why won't facets work on my factor?

messages.author: 5d3368b7e537b5dc
messages.subject: Why won't facets work on my factor?
parts:
Here's a self-contained example of some difficulty I've been having
constructing dataframes with factors that don't crash facet_wrap:

response <- c(rnorm(100), rnorm(100, mean=2, sd=2))
group <- factor(c(rep('group a', 100), rep('group b', 100)))
d <- data.frame(response, group)
rm(response, group)

So d is now a dataframe containing two columns, 'response' and
'group', where 'response' is normally distributed with mean=1, sd=1
for 'group a', and with mean=2, sd=2 for 'group b'.

Creating boxplots by group with the standard R graphics 'boxplot'
function works as expected:

boxplot(response ~ group, data=d)

And so does the analogous ggplot2 boxplot:

ggplot(data=d, aes(y=response, x=group)) + geom_boxplot()

But what doesn't seem to work is faceting by group:

# works fine:
ggplot(data=d, aes(x=response)) + geom_density()
# crashes:
ggplot(data=d, aes(x=response)) + geom_density() + facet_wrap(~group)

The above crashes with:

Error in tapply(1:nrow(data), splitv, list) :
arguments must have same length

Yet a very similar plot works fine on the 'diamonds' dataframe:

ggplot(data=diamonds, aes(x=carat)) + geom_density() +
facet_wrap(~color)

So what's the difference between my dataframe and 'diamonds'?
--
Max

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: Why won't facets work on my factor?
parts:
I have no idea what's happening with facet_wrap() in your example, but if you do the following it will work (at least it did for me)...

ggplot(data=d, aes(x=response)) + geom_density() + facet_grid(group ~ .)

OR

ggplot(data=d, aes(x=response)) + geom_density() + facet_grid(. ~ group)

Depends which orientation you want. 

HTH, 

Brandon

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Why won't facets work on my factor?
parts:
Hi:

To add to Brandon's suggestion (use facet_grid() instead of facet_wrap()), unfilled densities look pretty strange, so let's add some filled colors and suppress the automatic legend that ggplot() will produce:

ggplot(data = d, aes(x = response, fill = group)) + geom_density() +
    facet_grid( group ~ .) + scale_fill_hue(legend = FALSE)

I think this orientation is better for comparing the two groups rather than apposing them horizontally, but it's only an opinion...

HTH,
Dennis
